audit_findings.title: The 2027 refinancing could reset a large portion of the interest expense embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $350.0 million refinanced from 5.875% to 6.50%, increasing annual coupon expense by a computed $2.188 million, or 1.27% of $172.2 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: The higher recurring coupon reduces equity-level OE because interest expense is retained; debt principal remains context only.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate amounts of long-term debt maturities subsequent to September 27, 2025 are as follows: fiscal 2026: $-0-; fiscal 2027: $499.2 million (includes $149.2 million outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility); fiscal 2028: $-0- ; fiscal 2029: $11.7 million; fiscal 2030: $12.3 million; and thereafter: $706.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The refinancing uncertainty has been resolved: the 2027 notes were replaced in December 2025, and the revolver now matures in 2029. The demonstrated fixed-coupon increase is only $2.188 million annually. Even a proportional 1.27% reduction would lower the $34.27 base value by about $0.44 per unit, leaving the valuation conclusion and $23.99 buy-below comparison intact. Reported nine-month fiscal 2026 net interest expense was also $0.762 million below the comparable period because lower revolver rates offset part of the new coupon.
audit_findings.action: Replace the hypothetical refinancing assumption with the filed 6.50% notes, current revolver balance and 6.10% rate in the next routine OE roll-forward.

audit_findings.title: Required in-flight capital spending may be larger than the reinvestment charged by the valuation
audit_findings.magnitude: $75.0-$80.0 million disclosed fiscal 2026 program; $65.991 million spent through nine months plus $15.9 million anticipated for the remainder implies $81.891 million, or 47.6% of $172.2 million anchor OE; incremental required charge remains unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any maintenance or committed completion spending excluded from OE must reduce OE directly; growth spending supporting forecast growth must be reconciled with the RONTA-based reinvestment charge.
audit_findings.evidence: As we look ahead to fiscal 2026, our anticipated cash requirements include: (i) maintenance and growth capital expenditures of approximately $45.0 million for the propane segment; (ii) capital expenditures of approximately $30.0 to $35.0 million to support the construction and development efforts for our renewable energy platform; (iii) approximately $72.7 million of interest and income tax payments; and (iv) approximately $86.8 million of distributions to Unitholders, based on the current annualized rate of $1.30 per Common Unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending program is demonstrated, but an OE error is not yet demonstrated because the record does not classify the propane program fully between maintenance and growth or establish which renewable completion costs are avoidable. The scale is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: fiscal 2026 spending approaches half of anchor OE, while only $19.7 million of the first nine months' $66.0 million was labeled maintenance. A materially larger recurring or committed charge could consume the valuation's margin of safety.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile project-level fiscal 2026 capex to maintenance, committed completion and discretionary expansion; then rerun every scenario with required maintenance deducted from OE and growth capex reconciled to the 29.5% RONTA reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: Cash-settled unit-linked compensation creates a claim that rises with SPH's unit price
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.693 million latest disclosed PEP and LTIP liabilities ($10.164 million plus $11.529 million); $9.247 million of PEP, LTIP and DER expense in the first nine months of fiscal 2026; incremental price-linked cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: PEP and LTIP awards reduce OE through cash-settled compensation expense and remeasurement; they should not enter diluted shares, and an already accrued claim should not also be deducted from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon vesting, phantom units are automatically converted into cash equal to the average of the highest and lowest trading prices of the Partnership’s Common Units on the day prior to the vesting date.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-linked obligations and quarterly remeasurement are demonstrated, but understatement of the valuation is not. Historical OE retains compensation expense, and the latest liabilities are already accrued, so a separate bridge deduction could double count them. The record does not provide all outstanding award quantities, vesting assumptions and future grants needed to quantify the additional expense if units appreciate toward the DCF values.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the complete PEP, LTIP and DER award roll-forward and valuation sensitivities; project future service cost, price remeasurement and settlements through OE, exclude these awards from diluted units, and confirm that accrued amounts are not deducted twice.

audit_findings.title: The established multi-employer withdrawal obligation may not be captured by forward OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.440 million at June 27, 2026, equal to $0.26 per valuation share and 0.75% of $2.316 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If prior accounting expense removed the cost from forward OE, the unpaid withdrawal liability belongs in the equity bridge; otherwise actual withdrawal payments must reduce OE without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 27, 2025 and September 28, 2024, the Partnership’s estimated obligation for MEPP established withdrawals was $18,559 and $20,026, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether runoff is already captured remains unresolved, but even treating the entire latest obligation as an omitted equity claim would lower base value from $34.27 to about $34.01 per unit and the 30%-MOS buy-below level by about $0.18 to $23.81. That does not change the conclusion relative to the $17.52 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the payment schedule and OE treatment; deduct the latest unpaid balance once in the bridge if payments are not included in projected OE.

audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and latest balance-sheet perimeter are not fully synchronized
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.0 million total consideration for the two October 2025 acquisitions, equal to 1.04% of $2.316 billion base equity value and $0.36 per valuation share; acquired earnings contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted acquired earnings would understate OE, while omitted maintenance capital, working capital and financing costs would overstate it; post-acquisition units affect the denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 14, 2025, the Operating Partnership acquired the propane assets and operations of a propane retailer headquartered in California for $14,000, including $500 for non-compete consideration, plus working capital acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated because fiscal 2025 OE predates both California acquisitions while the balance sheet and share count are later. The latest 10-Q, however, states that their preliminary purchase-price allocations and operating results were not material. The combined transaction price is about 1% of base equity value, so the mismatch is not reasonably capable of reversing the large gap between estimated value and market price on the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Add a post-acquisition run-rate bridge using the fiscal 2026 segment results, including earnings, maintenance capex, working capital, financing and issued units, during the next anchor update.

audit_findings.title: Vehicle lease residual guarantees are a contingent claim beyond ordinary rent
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.813 million latest maximum exposure, equal to $0.63 per valuation share and 1.85% of $2.316 billion base equity value; filed fair value is de minimis
audit_findings.mechanism: Only an expected residual-value shortfall beyond ordinary lease expense would reduce OE or require an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Although the fair value of equipment at the end of its lease term has historically exceeded the guaranteed amounts, the maximum potential amount of aggregate future payments we could be required to make under these leasing arrangements, assuming the equipment is deemed worthless at the end of the lease term, was approximately $43.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss is demonstrated: equipment values have historically exceeded guarantees and the filed fair value of the obligation is de minimis. Even the implausible assumption that the entire maximum exposure were payable would lower base value only to about $33.64 per unit and the buy-below level to about $23.55, still well above the $17.52 price.
audit_findings.action: Monitor vehicle appraisals and guarantee maturities through fiscal 2033; rerun only if a probable shortfall becomes measurable, using the expected shortfall rather than the maximum exposure.
